method: Items are published only when an official primary source or at least two independent publishers support them.

items.headline: Chattogram Port Authority signs 15-year concession with DP World for New Mooring terminal
items.summary: On 8 October the Chattogram Port Authority and the UAE operator DP World signed a 15-year concession to run and modernise the New Mooring Container Terminal. Arab News reported investment of up to 10 billion taka over ten years and an upfront fee of 6 billion taka. TBS reported that the full agreement has not been published and that workers' leaders have questioned its value.
items.note: Investment figures differ in wording between outlets (TBS also cites a wider package of about 150 million US dollars).

sources.title: UAE's DP World to operate major terminal in Bangladesh's largest port
sources.evidence: Investment: up to 10 billion taka over the first 10 years; upfront fee of 6 billion taka

sources.title: DP World gets 15-year concession to operate New Mooring Container Terminal
sources.evidence: the full concession agreement has not been made public

items.headline: Regulator clears Rooppur nuclear Unit-1 to start first controlled reaction
items.summary: Bangladesh's Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority approved the B-2 licence on 8 October, allowing Unit-1 of the 1,200 MW Rooppur plant to reach first criticality. Its chairman said two further approvals are required before grid connection and that authorities hope to supply power by the end of the year.
items.note: The end-of-year grid date is a stated hope of the regulator, not a commitment.

sources.title: Authorities approve Rooppur Unit-1 to begin fission
sources.evidence: we are hopeful about starting power supply to the national grid by the end of this year

sources.title: Rooppur Unit-1 cleared for first nuclear reaction
sources.evidence: two more regulatory approvals would be required

items.headline: Dhaka seeks new Ganges water treaty with India before the current one expires on 12 December
items.summary: Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee said on 8 October that a new Ganges water-sharing treaty should be concluded before 12 December, when the 30-year agreement ends. He named restoring the guarantee clause of the 1977 agreement a priority. Talks continue through the Joint Rivers Commission, and he said Bangladesh is optimistic.
items.note: Only the Bangladeshi position is reported; India's stance is not covered in these sources.
